clue.text: One's dished after a henhouse raid ?

definitions.text: One's dished after a henhouse raid ?

parts.words: One's dished after a henhouse raid ?
parts.note: something stolen from the chicken run is 'poached', and the stolen item is then served up on a plate

explanation.surface: A fox or thief is fed after raiding the chicken coop.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on 'poached': stolen by a raider, and also a way of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked breakfast item simmered out of its shell, here also read as one taken illicitly from the hens.

clue.text: Scheme to make a gent noisy

annotationWithheld.why: Scheme to make a gent noisy (4): 'Scheme' defines PLAN but no parse of 'to make a gent noisy' was found (possibly a sound-play on Plantagenet); the scan confirms the text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Scheme to make a gent noisy

clue.text: One kind of spanner

parts.note: a spanner here is not a wrench but anything that spans a gap, such as a curved structure over a doorway or river

explanation.surface: A mechanic names a type of wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' suggests the tool; read it as 'thing that spans'.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved structure bridging an opening is something that spans it.

clue.text: It's no place for the homesick

definitions.text: It's no place for the homesick

parts.words: It's no place for the homesick
parts.note: 'homesick' is read as 'sick at home': people ill enough to be treated in a clinic room are not those who stay home

explanation.surface: Somewhere unsuitable for people pining for home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homesick' looks like longing for home; split it as the sick who are at home, who are not in a medical institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A room of beds in a medical institution is where the sick go when they are not nursed at home.

clue.text: Fruit, goes out of fashion

definitions.meaning: sweet brown fruits of a palm tree
a style that becomes old-fashioned is said to date

explanation.surface: Some fruit becomes unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm-tree fruits, and a verb meaning becomes old-fashioned or shows its age.

clue.text: She. takes the cart — her charges may be small.

definitions.text: She. takes the cart — her charges may be small.

parts.words: She. takes the cart — her charges may be small.
parts.note: a light two-wheeled trap was named after the woman who drove children in it; her 'charges' are the young pupils in her care, not fees

explanation.surface: A carter whose fees are modest.
explanation.walkthrough: A governess cart was a small pony trap; 'charges' suggests fees but means the children she looks after.
explanation.definitionFit: A private tutor of young children in a household, who gave her name to a small pony-drawn trap.

clue.text: Something to observe on a tramp in Australia'

definitions.text: Something to observe on a tramp in Australia

parts.words: Something to observe on a tramp in Australia
parts.note: an Australian itinerant carried his possessions rolled in a bundle on his back, so the bundle is visible on him

explanation.surface: A sight to look out for while hiking in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' suggests a walk; it is the vagrant, the Australian swagman, whose bedroll bundle gives him his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian term for the bedroll bundle carried by an itinerant worker.

clue.text: Time of occupation'

parts.note: 'occupation' suggests military occupation but means one's job, so the time is when one is at work

explanation.surface: A period when a country is occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the week or the hours one spends at one's job.

clue.text: Articles of coloured wear about town ?

definitions.text: Articles of coloured wear about town ?

parts.words: Articles of coloured wear about town ?
parts.note: the items of clothing are bands of a colour worn around the waist, read as open country zones encircling a town

explanation.surface: Colourful clothing seen around town.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a green belt is protected countryside ringing a town; the clue dresses it as clothing worn 'about' (around) the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Protected rural zones ringing a city, pictured as verdant waist-bands around it.

clue.text: The case for the prosecution ?

parts.note: 'case' is a grammatical case, and the one that suits a prosecutor is the one that sounds like accusing

explanation.surface: A lawyer's argument against the defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a trial; it is a grammatical case, the object case, whose name suggests accusing.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical case of a direct object, whose name comes from accusing, fitting a prosecutor.

clue.text: Language of some verse-mongers

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following word are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: The jargon used by certain poetasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of some' takes a run of letters from inside 'verse-mongers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland is an example of a language.

clue.text: It cannot safely be ignored

parts.note: describes a warning light or flag whose whole purpose is to alert people to peril

explanation.surface: A matter one overlooks at one's peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning sign of peril is something that must be heeded for safety.

clue.text: Roast pig was the subject of an Elian one

definitions.text: Roast pig was the subject of an Elian one

parts.words: Roast pig was the subject of an Elian one
parts.note: Charles Lamb, writing as Elia, wrote a comic essay upon roast pig

explanation.surface: Roast pork was the topic of a piece by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elian' means by Elia, the pen-name of Charles Lamb, whose Essays of Elia include A Dissertation upon Roast Pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A long formal essay or treatise on a subject, as in Lamb's title.

clue.text: The mark of a possessive form of address

definitions.meaning: the punctuation mark placed before the s in a word like 'John's'
in rhetoric, a speech turning aside to address someone absent or an abstraction

explanation.surface: The sign that marks a possessive way of addressing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the punctuation mark of ownership and a rhetorical figure of directly addressing an absent person.

clue.text: A breach in part.

parts.note: taken as written
a fraction is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: A partial breach.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a violation of a rule or law, a breach of it.

clue.text: Poll of balletomanes produces fruit

definitions.meaning: ... Poll is a comic ballet to music by Sullivan, so ballet fans know its Poll
a tropical fruit with a spiky skin

explanation.surface: A survey of ballet fans results in some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' suggests a survey; it is the heroine of the ballet Pineapple Poll (1951).
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical spiky fruit, and the first word of the ballet title Pineapple Poll.

clue.text: It's turned to use at sea and in the air

definitions.text: It's turned to use at sea and in the air

parts.words: It's turned to use at sea and in the air
parts.note: a bladed device is rotated to drive both ships and aircraft

explanation.surface: Something converted for use by navy and air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned to use' suggests converted; it is literally turned, spun, to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating bladed screw drives ships and aeroplanes.

clue.text: Take carriage to high-class quarter for a dance

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled carriage
U means upper-class
E, east, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Ride in a carriage to a smart district to go dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Baroque dance form in compound time, often ending a suite.

clue.text: Joiner's pay

definitions.meaning: a threaded fastener is something that joins, i.e. 'joiner is'

explanation.surface: A carpenter's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner's' reads as a carpenter's, but is 'joiner is', a fastener that joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded fastener joins pieces of wood; also slang for wages.

clue.text: Watchful employee goes after job, but no opening

indicators.note: the worker's word is placed after the trimmed task word
the word for a task loses its opening letter here

parts.note: taken as written
a servant is an employee

explanation.surface: An alert worker applies for a post but finds no vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No opening' suggests no vacancy; it drops the J from JOB, leaving OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert and quick to notice, as a careful watcher is.

clue.text: Legal office requiring 'some musical ability ?

parts.note: a recorder is a kind of judge and also a wind instrument, so the post seems to call for playing

explanation.surface: A judicial post that asks for musical skill.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a recorder is a part-time judge; the recorder is also a woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The post of a recorder, a part-time judge in the English courts.

clue.text: Simple soul was penniless

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the simple fellow meets a pieman but has no penny to buy a pie

explanation.surface: A naive person had no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' is the first word of the rhyme's character, Simple Simon, who told the pieman he had no penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the nursery-rhyme simpleton who could not pay the pieman.

clue.text: Pride is no deadly sin in his case

definitions.text: Pride is no deadly sin in his case

parts.words: Pride is no deadly sin in his case
parts.note: a pride is the collective noun for a group of big cats, so for this animal pride is just his family

explanation.surface: Arrogance is not a mortal sin for this man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' looks like the deadly sin; it is the word for a group of these big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat that lives in a group called a pride.

clue.text: Writes and folds

definitions.meaning: enclosures for sheep or other animals

explanation.surface: Someone writes and folds letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folds' suggests creasing paper; it means animal enclosures.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for writing, and enclosures for livestock.

clue.text: Father is not out to cause distress

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a batsman who is not out is still in

explanation.surface: Dad stays home and so causes worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering or hurt is distress.

clue.text: She was only a miner's daughter-alas, no more

definitions.text: She was only a miner's daughter-alas, no more

parts.words: She was only a miner's daughter-alas, no more
parts.note: the folk song tells of a forty-niner's daughter who drowned and was 'lost and gone for ever'

explanation.surface: A lament for a working man's daughter who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The American ballad 'Oh My Darling' describes a miner's daughter who drowned, so she is 'no more'.
explanation.definitionFit: The miner's daughter in the American song, who is lost and gone for ever.

clue.text: Irish lake bird.

definitions.meaning: a lough in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A bird on a lake in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lough of that name in Northern Ireland, and the white-tailed sea eagle.

clue.text: Garments once widely in evidence

parts.note: 'widely' refers to Victorian hooped skirts that stood out very wide, not to their popularity

explanation.surface: Clothes that were once commonly seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Widely' seems to mean commonly; it means the skirts were literally broad.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffened hooped petticoats of the Victorian era made skirts stand out wide.
